All green (213 files, 1975 tests — up 2 from the live scheduler job's test additions). Fixed.

**Root cause**: in `src/renderer/components/ui/EffectiveCards.tsx` (the "Guided" Settings view), clicking a left-rail item to jump to a section called `el.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' })`. Because that settings list is nested inside the app's outer layout scroll regions, `scrollIntoView()` walks up and scrolls **every** scrollable ancestor needed to bring the target fully into view — not just the settings pane's own list — which is exactly "it moves everything." Compounding it, the effect had no dependency array, so it re-ran after every unrelated re-render of the pane.

**Fix**: gave the settings list its own ref and scroll only that one container (`container.scrollBy({ top: delta, behavior: 'smooth' })`, computed from the target section's offset within it), and added the missing `[pendingScrollId]` dependency array so the effect only fires on an actual jump request.

Verified: `npm run typecheck` clean, `check-unstable-selectors.cjs` clean, full `npm run test:unit` green (213/213 files, 1975/1975 tests). Not committed — in the working tree per your standing rule.

Cleaned up the diagnostic test file. Final summary:

## Root cause, fully diagnosed

The reported bug ("scrolls to sections but moves everything and never resets") was real and caused by `EffectiveCards.tsx`'s left-rail "jump to section" handler calling `el.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' })` on the target `<section>`.

The critical detail I confirmed by instrumenting `#root.scrollTop` and `scrollIntoView` calls live in the running app: **`#root` has `overflow-y: hidden`** (it's never meant to scroll — all scrolling is supposed to happen in nested `overflow-auto` regions) **but genuinely overflows its content by ~800px**. `scrollIntoView()` doesn't respect `overflow: hidden` as a stopping boundary — it still walks up and sets `scrollTop` on any ancestor with `scrollHeight > clientHeight`, including hidden ones. So the browser scrolled `#root` itself by up to 269px, visibly dragging the tab strip, the left sidebar, and the whole app shell along with it. And because `#root` is never *supposed* to be scrollable, nothing in the app ever resets its `scrollTop` back to 0 — matching "never resets" exactly.

## The fix

Replaced the ancestor-walking `scrollIntoView()` with a scroll scoped to just the settings list's own container (`container.scrollBy({ top: delta, behavior: 'smooth' })`, computed from the target section's offset within that one container), and fixed the effect's missing `[pendingScrollId]` dependency array.
